subtype: Approach: making a feeding and cleaning schedule [Action]
passage: In the waiting room of the animal clinic, Ujjwal held his new puppy in his lap while the nurse, Binita, handed him a blank card. "Tell me a day with him," she said. Ujjwal wrote: 7 a.m., food. After school, walk. 6 p.m., food. Bedtime, check the water bowl. His mother nodded at each line. At home he pinned the card beside the front door with a red drawing pin. By the third evening his sister was reading it aloud before feeding time, and Ujjwal never had to remind anyone.

qa.q: Where did Ujjwal pin the card?
qa.a: He pinned the card beside the front door.

qa.q: What was Ujjwal feeling about the puppy as he wrote the card?
qa.a: Excited and committed, since he wrote out every part of a day with the puppy.

qa.q: What could the family do if a task on the card gets missed, and why?
qa.a: They could add tick boxes or take turns by day, so everyone can see what has been done.

qa.q: How might Binita see the card Ujjwal wrote?
qa.a: Binita probably sees a good start, since a written routine helps a new owner keep the puppy's care regular.

grounding: A boy with a new puppy writes a feeding, walking and water-check schedule and pins it where the family follows it.

subtype: Approach: making a feeding and cleaning schedule [Action]
passage: I'm Madhav, Ujjwal's cousin, and I stayed at their place the week they got Moti. For the first two days nobody knew who had fed the puppy. Ujjwal's mother fed Moti, then his father fed Moti again, and then nobody filled the water bowl. On the third evening Ujjwal sat at the dining table with a sketch pen and a sheet of paper. He wrote: FOOD 7 am and 6 pm. WALK after school. WATER BOWL check morning and night. Beside each line he drew little boxes for the days. He pinned it to the board by the front door, right where you take off your shoes. After that, whoever fed Moti ticked a box. I don't know if Ujjwal was proud, but he checked that sheet every time he came in.

qa.q: Where did Ujjwal pin the sheet?
qa.a: On the board by the front door, where you take off your shoes.

qa.q: Why did Ujjwal make the sheet?
qa.a: He seemed worried that Moti was being fed twice or left without water, and wanted the care to be steady.

qa.q: What else could help the schedule work?
qa.a: Writing a name beside each job, so everyone knows whose turn it is as well as what needs doing.

qa.q: How does Madhav see Ujjwal after the sheet?
qa.a: Madhav notices Ujjwal checking it every time he comes in, but is not sure whether Ujjwal feels proud.

grounding: A cousin watches a boy write a feeding, walking and water schedule for a new puppy and pin it by the door.

subtype: Approach: making a feeding and cleaning schedule [Action]
passage:
Saturday: The puppy arrived in a cardboard box. Mridul's father, Pankaj, fed her at breakfast; so did Dadi; so did Mridul after lunch. By evening the puppy had been sick on the rug.
Sunday: Mridul took a sheet of chart paper and wrote in big letters: FOOD, 7 in the morning and 6 in the evening. WALK, after school. WATER BOWL, check whenever you pass. He drew a column of boxes for each day and pinned it next to the front door, where everyone looks for keys.
Three weeks later: Pankaj came home late, glanced at the chart, saw the six o'clock box already ticked in Mridul's handwriting and put the food packet away. The puppy, fed once and walked, was asleep by nine.

qa.a: The puppy had been sick on the rug.

qa.q: What might Mridul have felt when the puppy was sick?
qa.a: Worried and a bit guilty, since everyone, including him, had fed her.

qa.q: What else could the family try along with the chart?
qa.a: Keep the food in one place beside the chart, so nobody feeds the puppy without seeing the ticks.

qa.q: What is the chart like for Pankaj three weeks later?
qa.a: Pankaj can see at a glance that the evening feed is done, so he does not feed the puppy again.

grounding: Across three weeks, a boy's feeding and walking chart by the door stops the family overfeeding their new puppy.
